Article Title: China Coast Guard vessel rams Philippine ship on mission to aid fishermen at sea
Article Text:
US rejects China's "nature reserve" plan at Scarborough Reef, backs Philippines

Philippine vessel damaged in collision

Tensions remain high in disputed waters

A China Coast Guard vessel collided with a Philippine government ship carrying out a fuel assistance mission for fishermen in the disputed South China Sea on Friday, damaging parts of the Philippine vessel, according to the Philippine Coast Guard.The incident took place about 54 nautical miles off Palawan province, where the Philippine Bureau of Fisheries and Aquatic Resources vessel BRP Datu Magat Salamat was delivering fuel assistance to Filipino fishermen.According to the Philippine Coast Guard, the Chinese vessel made several dangerous manoeuvres before hitting the Philippine ship at around 11.13 am local time."The China Coast Guard deliberately rammed a civilian government vessel on a humanitarian and livelihood mission," the Philippine Coast Guard said.The impact damaged the ship's starboard side, with sections of its railings bent, broken or torn away.Metal stanchions and support structures were also deformed, while fixtures and equipment on the deck were displaced. Debris was scattered across the vessel following the collision.The Philippine Coast Guard said the ship had been carrying out a mission intended to support Filipino fishermen operating in the area.China's embassy in Manila had not immediately responded to a request for comment on the incident.The latest confrontation adds to a series of incidents between Manila and Beijing in contested areas of the South China Sea.In July, the Philippines accused China of using water cannon against its government vessels near Scarborough Shoal.Manila also alleged that a Philippine Navy staff member was struck on the head with a wooden baton during an encounter near Second Thomas Shoal.The two countries have repeatedly confronted each other over competing claims in the South China Sea, with the Philippines maintaining that its vessels have the right to operate in areas within its claimed maritime zone.
Article Summary: Philippine Coast Guard says Chinese vessel made dangerous manoeuvres before collision. Vessel was carrying out fuel assistance mission for Filipino fishermen. Latest confrontation adds to a series of incidents between Manila and Beijing in contested areas of the South China Sea. In July, the Philippines accused China of using water cannon against its government vessels near Scarborough Shoal.

NEW DELHI: Former Union minister and BJP leader Ravneet Singh Bittu's convoy was attacked on Friday while he was on his way to Pathankot to attend a party event.According to Bittu's office, his security team has reportedly apprehended three individuals allegedly linked to the AAP."If anything happens to Ravneet Singh Bittu, the chief minister of Punjab and the DGP Punjab will be held responsible for his safety and security," Bittu's office said."Such incidents are a grave threat to democracy and the safety of political leaders; the Punjab government must immediately investigate this incident and ensure the safety of every political worker and leader," it added.Meanwhile, Bittu alleged that local MLA Sherry had sent the individuals to prevent him from participating in the yatra."Such incidents are a grave threat to democracy and the safety of political leaders," Bittu said.BJP national president Nitin Nabin is scheduled to flag off the party’s ‘Nasha Mukt Punjab Yatra’ from Pathankot on Friday. The yatra will cover 4,000 kilometres across all 117 assembly constituencies before concluding in Jalandhar on September 30.Nabin said the party is launching a movement against drug abuse in Punjab, alleging that the state’s youth have been pushed towards addiction and promising to undertake the campaign alongside families affected by the menace.Speaking to ANI, Nabin said, "I believe that the youth of Punjab—descendants of hardworking farming families, heirs to a rich culture and a thriving industrial sector that was once a source of pride for the entire nation—have been pushed into the clutches of addiction and left completely directionless. This generation could have been a symbol of honour for Punjab and a driving force in shaping its future; instead, they were led astray."I also believe that political parties in the state exploited the drug issue merely to gain power, only to treat the drug trade as a business venture or a source of profit once in office, allowing it to flourish under political patronage. The Bharatiya Janata Party is now launching a movement against this. Following the nationwide mass movement against drugs initiated by the PM on August 2nd, the Punjab BJP is organizing a campaign to take a stand against this menace. We will undertake this journey alongside families who have lost loved ones and deeply understand this pain and suffering," he further said.
Article Summary: Former Union minister Ravneet Singh Bittu's convoy was attacked on Friday while he was on his way to Pathankot to attend a party event. His security team has reportedly apprehended three individuals allegedly linked to the AAP. Nabin said the party is launching a movement against drug abuse in Punjab, alleging that the state's youth have been pushed towards addiction.

Article Title: 'See how many allies of Pakistan were in that room': Omar Abdullah praises Centre over Pahalgam condemnation at Brics
Article Text:
Omar praises Centre for Brics

NEW DELHI: Jammu and Kashmir chief minister Omar Abdullah on Tuesday heaped praise on the foreign policy of PM Narendra Modi-led Centre and recently held Brics Summit in Delhi. Omar Abdullah said the Brics declaration condemning Pakistan-backed Pahalgam terror attack was a major diplomatic win.J&K CM remarks came after India hosted the 18th Brics Summit in New Delhi, bringing together several world leaders, including Chinese President Xi Jinping and Russian President Vladimir Putin.The National Conference leader particularly highlighted the inclusion of the Pahalgam terror attack in the Brics New Delhi Declaration, pointing out that the statement came in the presence of countries that share close ties with Pakistan."That is something for the Government of India, and particularly for the foreign ministry, to talk about. The fact that Pahalgam itself was condemned is a big thing. Please see how many allies of Pakistan were in that room. Therefore, for even Pahalgam to be mentioned by name, that in itself is a success of our foreign policy," Omar Abdullah said.J&K CM Omar also welcomed steps aimed at easing tensions along India’s fronts with Pakistan and China.Reacting to the ministry of defence’s report on the operational situation along the Northern Front, he said any move to reduce troop deployments along the Line of Actual Control (LAC) or Line of Control (LoC) would be a positive development, particularly for people living in border areas."Anything that reduces tension along the Line of Control or the Line of Actual Control is a good step, particularly for those people who live close to it. We know that living near the LoC or LAC is extremely difficult for people. If there is any step that reduces deployments along the Line of Actual Control, that is a good step. Similarly, we hope that, over time, things will also get better along the Line of Control," he added.The comments came days after the Brics Summit concluded in the national capital. Prime Minister Narendra Modi announced that the New Delhi Declaration had been unanimously adopted and called the gathering as a huge summit.Days ago, senior Congress leader Shashi Tharoor backed the Brics Summit as an important diplomatic opportunity for India, appearing to differ with party colleague P Chidambaram, who questioned whether recent Brics meetings have produced tangible benefits.Tharoor highlighted the diplomatic value of India hosting leaders from across the Brics grouping and its partner countries, stressing the importance of such engagements for New Delhi.Chidambaram, however, had questioned the outcomes of recent Brics summits.“I don't think the last two or three Brics summits have resulted in tangible benefits or tangible results.”“In fact, we are part of Brics, we are part of SCO, we are part of G20, and we are part of Quad. What benefits are we getting out of that? I can't see. In the last two or three summits, I didn't see any benefits. Earlier, the Brics Summits resulted in some tangible benefits,” he added.Chidambaram’s remarks triggered a political response from the BJP, which accused the Congress of questioning an event that, it said, reflected India’s growing standing on the global stage.
Article Summary: J&K CM Omar Abdullah heaped praise on the foreign policy of PM Narendra Modi-led Centre. He said the Brics declaration condemning Pakistan-backed Pahalgam terror attack was a major diplomatic win. Omar also welcomed steps aimed at easing tensions along India's fronts with Pakistan and China.

Article Title: ‘Umar Khalid is a nationalist’: B K Hariprasad’s remark sparks BJP attack
Article Text:
Karnataka Congress president B K Hariprasad called jailed activist Umar Khalid a nationalist.





BENGALURU: Karnataka Congress president B K Hariprasad Tuesday called jailed activist Umar Khalid a “nationalist” and criticised Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad ( ABVP ) for opposing a proposed screening of a documentary on him at National Law School of India University (NLSIU).“ABVP has no right to speak about Khalid because ABVP adores Nathuram Godse, who is anti-national and the first terrorist of the country,” Hariprasad said.The remarks came after ABVP in Bengaluru demanded cancellation of the proposed screening of filmmaker Lalit Vachani’s documentary, ‘Prisoner No. 626710 is Present’, at NLSIU. The documentary was scheduled to be screened Monday by the law and society committee, a student organisation at the university. NLSIU later said it had to reschedule the event due to “logistical and security considerations”.The screening was to express solidarity with Khalid and to mark six years since his imprisonment without trial under Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act in connection with the 2020 Delhi riots.BJP hit back at Hariprasad’s remarks, calling them deeply condemnable. In New Delhi, Sambit Patra, MP, linked Hariprasad’s remarks to Congress’ past interactions with Kashmiri separatist leader Yasin Malik.“Just think about it: this is the same Umar Khalid,” Patra said. “During the Citizenship Amendment Act protests in Feb 2020, so many people were killed in Delhi. A case was filed under UAPA. The matter was heard across multiple courts; even in Feb 2026, the Supreme Court rejected Umar Khalid’s bail plea. Look at the sympathy Congress party harbours for the very same Umar Khalid.”Patra also attacked Congress party over its meetings with Yasin Malik, alleging the party had reduced itself to “appeasement”.
Article Summary: Karnataka Congress president B K Hariprasad called jailed activist Umar Khalid a ‘nationalist’ He criticised Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad ( ABVP ) for opposing a proposed screening of a documentary on him at National Law School of India University.

Article Title: ‘May your service be accompanied by good health’: Bangladesh PM Rahman wishes PM Modi on birthday
Article Text:
Bangladesh PM Tarique Rahman extends birthday greetings to PM Modi, wishes him good health and high spirit

Greeting from across nation and beyond

NEW DELHI: Bangladesh Prime Minister Tarique Rahman wished Prime Minister Narendra Modi on his 76th birthday on Thursday, as Dhaka seeks to reset ties with New Delhi.“Warmest birthday wishes to Prime Minister @narendramodi. Wishing you many happy returns of the day. May your dedicated service to the people of India always be accompanied by good health and high spirit,” Rahman posted on X.PM Modi responded by thanking Rahman for his message.“Thank you, Prime Minister Tarique Rahman, for your warm wishes. I deeply appreciate your kind words,” he said.The exchange comes at a time when Bangladesh is seeking to move away from the strained ties of the previous 18 months. State Minister for Foreign Affairs Humaiun Kobir said on Sunday that Dhaka wanted to “reset” its relationship with India and establish a new engagement centred on mutual interests.Relations had deteriorated during Muhammad Yunus’s interim administration, which came to power after the Sheikh Hasina government was toppled in August 2024. Hasina left Bangladesh for India after her ouster, and her continued stay there has remained a major point of friction, with Dhaka repeatedly seeking her extradition.Rahman’s Bangladesh Nationalist Party won the February 12 election, held without Hasina’s Awami League, which has since been disbanded. His government has maintained its demand for Hasina’s extradition, while the former prime minister has said she plans to return to Bangladesh to face legal proceedings.Dhaka has also indicated that Rahman could visit India once the two governments agree on a suitable time and schedule.Rahman’s message was among birthday greetings sent to PM Modi by political leaders, foreign governments, diplomats and public figures on Thursday.Russian President Vladimir Putin sent his wishes and, according to the Russian Embassy in New Delhi, described PM Modi as a leader with “great authority on the global stage”. Putin also thanked Modi for the “warm and cordial welcome and hospitality” during his recent visit to New Delhi for the BRICS summit.Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni described the Prime Minister as a “friend” and said she looked forward to further strengthening India-Italy relations. Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said Modi’s leadership had “transformed India into a world power” and described the India-Israel relationship as an “unprecedented partnership”.The US Embassy in India also conveyed birthday greetings on behalf of President Donald Trump.Opposition leaders, including Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge, Rahul Gandhi, Akhilesh Yadav, Mayawati and Jammu and Kashmir Chief Minister Omar Abdullah, joined the birthday wishes.PM Modi was born on September 17, 1950, in Vadnagar, Gujarat. He became Gujarat chief minister in 2001 and prime minister in 2014, and is set to complete 25 years in public office on October 7.The BJP has launched a month-long ‘Seva Sankalp Abhiyan’ to mark the occasion, with service and public outreach programmes across the country. In Delhi, about 1.25 lakh earthen lamps were lit at Kartavya Path as part of the ‘Ashirwad Ka Diya’ campaign.Several film personalities, including Shah Rukh Khan, Salman Khan, Chiranjeevi, Ram Charan, Mahesh Babu and Kamal Haasan, also wished the prime minister.
Article Summary: PM Modi was born on September 17, 1950, in Vadnagar, Gujarat. He became Gujarat chief minister in 2001 and prime minister in 2014. The BJP has launched a month- long ‘Seva Sankalp Abhiyan’ to mark the occasion.

Article Title: TMC vs TMC: EC bars both factions from using party symbol, name in West Bengal assembly bypolls
Article Text:
TMC vs TMC: EC bars both factions from using party symbol, name in Bengal bypolls

NEW DELHI: The Election Commission on Thursday barred both rival Trinamool Congress (TMC) factions from using the party's name and reserved election symbol in the upcoming West Bengal Assembly bypolls, according to an interim order.The decision comes ahead of the October 6 bypolls in Nandigram and Rejinagar, where factions led by Mamata Banerjee and Ritabrata Banerjee had fielded candidates while staking claim to the TMC identity and its twin-flowers-on-grass symbol.The poll panel has been hearing competing claims from the two factions over control of the party, its name and election symbol. Both sides have submitted documents and appeared before the Commission during the proceedings.The dispute reached the Election Commission in July after the rival factions staked competing claims to control of the TMC. The Commission subsequently sought responses on issues including organisational control, authorised signatories, party assets, name and election symbol.The issue gained urgency after the EC announced the Nandigram and Rejinagar bypolls for October 6. With nominations closing on September 16, the Commission faced a deadline to determine how the rival factions would contest the elections.The Commission held separate meetings with representatives of both factions on September 12.The Mamata faction was represented by Derek O'Brien, Kalyan Banerjee, Sagarika Ghose, Saket Gokhale and advocate Abhinav Singh. The Ritabrata faction was represented by Ritabrata Banerjee, Akhruzzaman, Arup Roy, Chandrima Bhattacharya and Riju Datt.Both sides maintained that they represented the legitimate TMC and sought recognition of their claim to the party name and symbol.The Mamata faction argued that Banerjee remained the party chairperson and that the national working committee was still within its five-year term.The rival faction contended that the party constitution provided for a three-year term, which it said had ended in February 2025.On September 13, the EC sought final submissions from both factions by 3 pm on September 16, the nomination deadline for the two bypolls. The Commission indicated that another hearing could be held on September 17.At the time, the Mamata faction said that in the absence of an interim order, it would contest using the original TMC symbol. The Ritabrata faction maintained that the EC alone could decide which side was entitled to use the party name and symbol.On September 15, TOI reported that the Commission was likely to issue an interim ruling on September 17. The EC subsequently scheduled another hearing with both factions on Thursday.
Article Summary: The Election Commission has barred both rival Trinamool Congress factions from using the party's name and reserved election symbol. The decision comes ahead of the October 6 bypolls in Nandigram and Rejinagar. The dispute reached the Election Commission in July after the rival factions staked competing claims to control of the party.

Article Title: SC slams builders for anonymous complaints against judges
Article Text:
We will direct a CBI inquiry into these complaints to find out who are behind it,” said bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant &d Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana

NEW DELHI: Supreme Court Thursday took a serious view of a large number of anonymous complaints received by it against judges, amici curiae and counsel after SC turned up the heat on several realtors and builders for misusing subvention schemes, duping homebuyers, delaying projects and refusing to refund the money invested."We will direct a CBI inquiry into these complaints to find out who are behind it," said a bench of Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana, after additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati handed over the CBI status report on its investigations into builders who had misused subvention schemes in collusion with bank officials, resulting in homebuyers paying EMIs without any hope of getting their dream homes even after waiting for decades.CJI Kant asked, "In these matters, who are the counsel representing the builders? You (builders) have started sending anonymous complaints to us? You people do not know what kind of stubborn people we are."Turning to Bhati, the CJI said on the next hearing date, "we will give you another set of complaints. You inquire into them and find out who the people responsible for writing these are. Most of them will be builders, we assume, and, of course, some counsel who have ill-advised them"."We will catch hold of them. Do you think we will get cowed down by this? We will direct CBI to register an FIR and investigate them. We will take it to the logical conclusion," the bench said.In April last year, SC had ordered a CBI investigation into the abuse of subvention agreements by builders and banks. At the last hearing, Bhati had informed SC that CBI had registered 50 FIRs and completed probes in 18 of them, filing 17 chargesheets and a closure report before competent courts.She said several bank officials were found to have been in collusion with the builders and were named among the accused in the chargesheets, and the agency had invoked provisions of Prevention of Corruption Act against them. CBI has sought sanctions for prosecuting bank officials from State Bank of India, Bank of India, Uco Bank, HDFC Bank and ICICI Bank.SC had directed banks to expeditiously grant sanction for prosecution and said failure to do so would warrant submission of an explanation before the court.SC had also directed CBI to conduct a thorough investigation into allegations of misrepresentation and other irregularities by entities known as "Ozone group in Karnataka, Maharashtra, Tamil Nadu; Vivansaa in Bengaluru; Rudra Buildwell Pvt Ltd in Greater Noida; and Omaxe group in Chandigarh". It had sought a separate probe status report in this regard.
Article Summary: Supreme Court Thursday took a serious view of a large number of anonymous complaints received by it against judges, amici curiae and counsel. SC turned up the heat on several realtors and builders for misusing subvention schemes, duping homebuyers, delaying projects and refusing to refund money.

Article Title: NIA court issues NBWs against 2 Pak-based LeT commanders
Article Text:
NIA alleged that Khalid and Saifullah had worked as LeT commanders in Kashmir before moving to Pakistan

JAMMU: A special NIA court in Jammu has issued non-bailable warrants (NBWs) against two Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) commanders for evading arrest in terror cases.Justice Prem Sagar passed separate orders on Sept 8 against the duo — Khalid alias Lala Huzaifa alias Bakkarwali, a resident of Pakistan’s South Punjab province; and Saifullah alias Sajid Jatt alias Ali Bhai alias Habibullah Malik (also known by several other aliases), a resident of Pakistan’s Kasur district.NIA alleged that Khalid and Saifullah had worked as LeT commanders in Kashmir before moving to Pakistan, from where they were currently providing weapons, money, and directions to ultras operating in Kashmir. While Khalid was active in Ganderbal and Bandipora districts, Saifullah — a designated terrorist listed in the Fourth Schedule of UAPA — operated in Kulgam between 2005 and 2007, NIA stated. The investigation also revealed communication IDs allegedly linked to Saifullah, according to court records.The proceedings stem from a case wherein J&K Police intercepted a motorbike at Gujar Tent, Pandach, Srinagar, during naka checking on March 31, 2026. A Chinese grenade and 15 live rounds/cartridges were allegedly seized from the rider, Mohammad Naqeeb Bhat of Batpora, Srinagar. An FIR was registered at Zakoora PS under provisions of the UAPA, Arms Act and Explosive Substances Act. The case was transferred to NIA in April.DSP Amit Sharma said NIA moved applications before the special court seeking NBWs against Khalid and Saifullah. As their attendance could not be secured through ordinary means, the court granted the requests. The NBW against Khalid was forwarded to DIG, NIA Jammu, for execution, while Saifullah’s NBW was sent to SSP Kulgam.
Article Summary: A special NIA court in Jammu has issued non-bailable warrants (NBWs) against two Pakistan-based Lashkar-e-Taiba (LeT) commanders. NIA alleged that Khalid and Saifullah had worked as LeT commanders in Kashmir before moving to Pakistan, from where they were currently providing weapons, money, and directions to ultras operating in Kashmir.

Article Title: 2 Jaish terrorists killed in Udhampur
Article Text:
An Army-CRPF-J&K police team launched the operation in Brattal bordering Kathua district

JAMMU: Two Jaish-e-Mohammad terrorists were shot dead and a suspected overground worker was detained Thursday after security forces tracked down a hideout in rain-soaked forests of Udhampur district in J&K’s Jammu division, seizing assault rifles, a pistol and grenades.An Army-CRPF-J&K police team launched the operation in Brattal bordering Kathua district after inputs led forces to cordon off a target area around 9pm Wednesday. “A few rounds of gunfire and grenade blasts were heard shortly after,” an official said.The terrorists resumed firing Thursday morning, apparently trying to break the cordon, but were killed in return fire. White Knight Corps said a mop-up operation was underway using sniffer dogs and aerial surveillance to check for any remaining terrorists.Police identified the slain terrorists as Saddam and Mustafa. Forces found an AK-series rifle with four magazines, an M-4 carbine with three magazines, a Glock pistol with two magazines and four grenades on them.
Article Summary: Two Jaish-e-Mohammad terrorists were shot dead and a suspected overground worker was detained. Security forces tracked down a hideout in rain-soaked forests of Udhampur district in J&K’s Jammu division, seizing assault rifles, a pistol and grenades.

Article Title: ‘Enough is enough’: Delhi HC raps DU, police over violence ahead of DUSU polls
Article Text:
Delhi HC seeks report from DU, police over DUSU violence

NEW DELHI: The Delhi high court on Thursday took strong exception to incidents of violence during campaigning for the Delhi University Students' Union (DUSU) elections, warning that it could stay the counting of votes and declaration of results if it is not satisfied with the response of Delhi University, Delhi Police and the Centre.“Enough is enough,” the court said while hearing the matter concerning violence during DUSU election campaigning in Delhi University's North Campus.The court sought reports from Delhi University, Delhi Police and the government by Friday on the steps taken to control the violence.It warned that if it was not satisfied with the responses and action taken, it would pass an order staying the counting of votes and declaration of the election results.The court also observed: "Democracy can't be converted into a criminal society."The directions came a day before the scheduled DUSU elections, amid concerns over incidents of violence during the campaign.
Article Summary: The Delhi high court took strong exception to incidents of violence during campaigning for the Delhi University Students' Union (DUSU) elections. The court sought reports from Delhi University, Delhi Police and the government by Friday. It warned that if it was not satisfied with the responses and action taken, it would pass an order staying the counting of votes and declaration of the election results.

Article Title: 'Your leadership has transformed India into a world power': Netanyahu greets PM Modi on 76th birthday
Article Text:
Israel PM Benjamin Netanyahu

Israeli prime minister Benjamin Netanyahu on Thursday extended birthday greetings to Prime Minister Narendra Modi, describing the India-Israel relationship as an “unprecedented partnership” and saying the friendship between the two countries had “never been stronger”.Birthday greetings poured in from across the world, with foreign leaders, envoys and diplomatic missions highlighting India’s bilateral partnerships and Modi’s role in strengthening ties. Russian president Vladimir Putin praised his contribution to the “special and privileged strategic partnership” between India and Russia, while Italian prime minister Giorgia Meloni wished Modi “health, energy, and success”.“Happy birthday, Narendra!” Netanyahu wrote in a post on X, alongside an image of the two leaders. “Your leadership has transformed India into a world power. Together, we have built an unprecedented partnership between our two great democracies.”The Modi-Netanyahu bonhomie has become a prominent feature of India-Israel ties, with both leaders repeatedly highlighting their personal friendship and political trust.Their meetings and public exchanges have highlighted a relationship that extends beyond formal diplomacy into close strategic cooperation.“The friendship between Israel and India has never been stronger, and together we will take it to even greater heights,” he added, wishing Modi “many more years of leadership, health and fulfillment”.India and Israel established full diplomatic relations in 1992, while PM Modi’s July 2017 visit to Israel elevated the relationship to a strategic partnership. Netanyahu followed with a visit to India in January 2018.The relationship now covers defence, security, technology, agriculture, water, innovation, trade and other areas. During PM Modi’s visit to Israel in February 2026, Netanyahu described him as “my dear friend” and said, “You are more than a friend; you are a brother in many respects.” He also said, “Israel is stronger than ever and India is stronger than ever.”Netanyahu's birthday message came days after India hosted the 18th BRICS Summit in New Delhi, where the grouping adopted a New Delhi Declaration that included strong references to the Israel-Lebanon conflict and the Gaza war.On Lebanon, BRICS leaders said, “We welcome the ceasefire in Lebanon” and called for full implementation of UN Security Council Resolution 1701. The declaration also called on Israel to “withdraw its occupying forces from all of the Lebanese territories, in which they remain”.That diplomatic contrast has not, so far, translated into a visible rupture in India-Israel ties. Netanyahu’s latest message instead points to continued political engagement, while New Delhi maintains separate tracks with Israel, Arab countries and the wider BRICS grouping.
Article Summary: Israel PM Benjamin Netanyahu extends birthday greetings to India's PM Narendra Modi. Netanyahu describes India-Israel relationship as an ‘unprecedented partnership’ PM Modi’s July 2017 visit to Israel elevated the relationship to a strategic partnership.

Article Title: Houthis, Saudis, Iran - and the future of Middle Eastern oil
Article Text:
Houthi fighters stand in front of what they say is a downed Saudi jet, at a location given as Yemen

What’s the latest Houthi offensive all about?

Why is this a serious headache?

In a lightning offensive last week, Yemen’s Houthis took over much of the country’s Red Sea coast, threatening shipping in the vital sea lane that had emerged as an alternative to Strait of Hormuz in the Persian Gulf. Houthis have been fighting a Saudi-led military coalition for a decade, although a 2022 UN-brokered truce halted their attacks on Saudi territory. But the Houthis’ latest move has once again sent oil prices north of the $100 per barrel mark, adding another front to the wider US-Israel war against Iran. Here’s the lowdown on why the Houthis’ Red Sea threat matters, how this puts Saudi Arabia in a serious pickle, and what it means for the Iran war:The offensive saw Houthis take over key parts of Yemen’s Red Sea coast. This adds weight to the Houthi threat to shipping in the vital sea lane. In fact, Houthis had earlier declared a blockade of Saudi ships in the region. Now they can seriously enforce this. Their mere presence along the coastline will make shippers jittery and raise insurance costs.With Strait of Hormuz effectively locked up by Iran and US, Red Sea had emerged as a vital alternative route, especially for energy trade out of the region.Saudi Arabia’s East-West pipeline was working at full capacity, transporting around 7 million barrels of oil daily across the breadth of the peninsula to the Red Sea port of Yanbu. This was a crucial lifeline for the global energy trade that had been severely restricted following the outbreak of the Iran war in Feb. But that East-West pipeline was hit by a drone attack last week — blamed on Iran-backed Shia militias in Iraq — to coincide with the Houthi advance on the Red Sea coast. Both operations seem to have been coordinated to put the choke on Red Sea shipping, which has to pass through the narrow Bab el-Mandeb strait that Houthis can now theoretically shut down.The timing of all this is not a coincidence. Actually, when the Iran war began, among Iran’s proxies in the region, Houthis held back. But in July, following the state funeral of Iran’s former supreme leader Ali Khamenei, an Iranian plane carrying the Houthi delegation back to Yemen was threatened by Saudi Arabia. Riyadh did not want that plane to land, and bombed the airport in the Houthi-controlled Yemeni capital of Sanaa. But that plane landed anyway.Following the episode, Houthi rhetoric against the Saudis flared up. But the key development that may have pushed Houthis into action could be the American blockade of Iranian ports and shipping in Persian Gulf.By many estimates, that blockade appears to be working, and putting enormous pressure on the Iranian economy. Tehran is unable to push out its own oil, the Iranian rial has tanked, and Iranians have actually taken to saving eggs instead of hard cash. Plus, this is a strategy that plays into America’s strength — it can carry out a naval blockade for a far longer period than a continuous kinetic war against Iran.So, Iran, through the Houthi action, is sending the message that if oil can’t pass through Hormuz, any alternative routes, including through the Red Sea, will also be shut. In short, the energy trade in the region is handcuffed till the war is resolved.What do Houthis want? The Houthis’ main grievance is against the Saudis, whom they have been fighting since 2015. But, of course, as a member of Iran’s so-called ‘Axis of Resistance’, they are now being heavily supported by Tehran in terms of material and intelligence inputs. Especially since the Gaza and Iran wars have seen Tehran’s two main proxies in Hezbollah and Hamas take a huge battering. So, the Iranian Axis appears to be undergoing a recalibration, with Houthis and Iran-backed militias in Iraq taking a more leading role among the proxies. Ultimately Houthis want legitimacy. Their attacks against Saudi Arabia — they reportedly fired a drone at Mecca earlier this week — raise their profile. Their capture of the Red Sea coast gives them international attention. And these, in turn, see them emerge as the primary force in Yemen, instead of the internationally backed Yemeni transition govt. Obviously, all of this helps Iran.Because US has refused to directly intervene against Houthis this time. Washington is providing diplomatic and advisory support to Riyadh, but not much else. Saudis want missile and drone interceptors. But US stocks are running low, thanks to its war with Iran. Saudi Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman has similarly sought assistance from Egypt and UK. But no one is rushing military aid to Riyadh. Interestingly, even the recently inked Mecca Pact between Saudi Arabia, Turkiye, and Pakistan hasn’t been activated.First, Houthis prove Iran’s Axis of Resistance is changing shape, with the Yemini militia taking a leading role. This has implications for both the Iran war, and security in Red Sea and Horn of Africa region. And second, alternative routes to Hormuz for energy transit, whether through sea or pipelines, are also not fully secure. They can be targeted by a host of Iran-backed militias in the region. This puts West Asia’s dominance in global energy supply under a serious cloud, perhaps forcing the international community to look for alternatives away from the region.
Article Summary: Houthis have been fighting a Saudi-led military coalition for a decade. The Houthis’ latest move has once again sent oil prices north of the $100 per barrel mark. Red Sea had emerged as an alternative to Strait of Hormuz in the Persian Gulf.

Article Title: 'Prisoner No. 626710 is Present': CBFC flags Umar Khalid film screening at IIIT-Hyderabad
Article Text:
Umar Khalid





HYDERABAD: The Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) objected to the proposed screening of a documentary on jailed activist Umar Khalid at IIIT-Hyderabad, saying screening an uncertified film would violate the Cinematograph Act unless an exemption had been granted, according to news agency PTI reported.The documentary, "Prisoner No. 626710 is Present", directed by filmmaker Lalit Vachani, was proposed to be screened by a group of students at the institute's KRB Auditorium at 8 pm on Friday. Sources said the students have now decided to cancel the screening."Public screening of a documentary film that has not yet been certified by the CBFC is a violation of the Cinematograph Act unless a specific exemption has been sought under the Act," the CBFC posted on X.Tagging IIIT-Hyderabad, the CBFC said the institute's authorities "may take note for necessary action".The CBFC functions under the Union Information and Broadcasting Ministry.IIIT-H, however, distanced itself from the proposed screening, saying neither the institute nor any of its recognised student bodies had organised or hosted a screening of an uncertified film.In a statement, the institute said it "categorically clarifies that neither the Institute nor any of its recognised student clubs, cells or organisations has organised or hosted any screening of any film uncertified by the Central Board of Film Certification"."IIIT Hyderabad has established processes governing official events and activities on campus, and any claim attributing an unauthorised or unrelated activity to the Institute or its recognised student bodies is factually incorrect," it said.The institute said students and faculty from its large and diverse community may meet or interact with people in their individual capacities."Such personal interactions or visits, where they occur, should not be construed as Institute-organised events, nor do they represent the views or activities of the Institute," it said.The development comes days after a proposed screening of the same documentary at the National Law School of India University (NLSIU) in Bengaluru was postponed following opposition from the RSS-affiliated Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP).The NLSIU screening, organised by its student-run Law and Society Committee, was scheduled for September 14 to mark Political Prisoners' Day and six years of Khalid's incarceration.The ABVP had demanded that the screening be cancelled, alleging that allowing it would amount to using the campus for political propaganda.The student committee later postponed the programme citing "logistical and security considerations". It maintained that it was not backing out because of pressure and said the screening would be held later in the trimester."Prisoner No. 626710 is Present" centres on Khalid, a former Jawaharlal Nehru University research scholar who was arrested in September 2020 in connection with the alleged larger conspiracy behind the northeast Delhi riots.Khalid has been charged under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act and other provisions in the case and has remained in custody since his arrest.The invitation for the proposed IIIT-H screening said it was planned on the occasion of "Political Prisoners' Day".It also referred to the anniversary of the death of revolutionary Jatindra Nath Das, a comrade of Bhagat Singh who died after a prolonged hunger strike in Lahore jail in 1929.
Article Summary: The Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) objected to the proposed screening of a documentary on jailed activist Umar Khalid at IIIT-Hyderabad. The documentary, "Prisoner No. 626710 is Present", directed by filmmaker Lalit Vachani, was proposed to be screened by a group of students at the institute's KRB Auditorium at 8 pm on Friday. Sources said the students have now decided to cancel the screening.

Article Title: Nolan Wells case update: Court hears disturbing allegations before judge orders suspect jailed without bond
Article Text:
Nolan Wells(Image via Getty Images)

Edward James Porter remains jailed after alleged threats

What the court heard about the alleged threats

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

A federal judge in Mississippi has ordered Edward James Porter to remain in custody without bond after prosecutors challenged his release in a case involving alleged threats against a witness connected to the investigation into Nolan Xavier Wells’ death. The ruling followed an emergency hearing where an FBI agent described repeated calls and threats allegedly directed at Bart Edmiston Jr. and his family.U.S. District Judge Taylor McNeel ruled that Porter should remain behind bars while his federal case proceeds. Prosecutors had sought an emergency hearing after another federal judge in Illinois had granted him bond.During the Sept. 9 hearing, FBI Task Force Agent Christopher Kloc testified about a series of calls allegedly made by Porter on July 31. According to the testimony reported by the Sun Herald, Porter allegedly used Pinger to disguise his actual phone number and make the calls appear to originate from Moss Point, Mississippi.Kloc said Porter made 12 calls to Bart Edmiston Jr. and his father over roughly three hours. Prosecutors allege that the calls included threats against the family.Edmiston Jr., 21, is a friend of Nolan Wells and currently plays football at the University of Wyoming.His name appeared in a Mississippi Department of Marine Resources incident report after he helped tow a boat connected to the events surrounding Wells' disappearance.The threats came weeks after Wells, 18, disappeared following a Fourth of July trip to Horn Island off Mississippi's Gulf Coast. His body was found on July 6. Authorities have not charged anyone in connection with Wells' death.The testimony presented a troubling picture of the alleged communications. Kloc told the court that Porter had Edmiston Jr.'s childhood address in Ocean Springs and allegedly sent it to him by text.According to testimony, Porter also contacted Edmiston Sr. while he was undergoing a medical procedure. The FBI agent said Porter allegedly threatened the older man, his household and responding police officers.Porter later allegedly told Edmiston Jr. that he was outside the family's Ocean Springs home and threatened to kill the family, according to the testimony.The judge also considered Porter's previous criminal record. The court was told that he had faced numerous violent criminal charges over the years, including allegations involving assault, assault with a deadly weapon and domestic violence. The pretrial report also showed that he had forfeited bond 13 times and had a pending fugitive-from-justice charge.Porter was unemployed and living at a homeless shelter when he was arrested in Illinois. His sister offered to let him stay with her, but she told the court she would be away at work during the day and could not supervise him.McNeel ultimately determined that Porter presented a flight risk and a danger to the victims and community. The judge concluded that detention was necessary because available release conditions could not reasonably guarantee safety or ensure Porter's appearance in future proceedings.Porter is not the only person facing federal allegations connected to threats surrounding the Wells investigation. Brandon Ephriam Washington of Jacksonville, Florida, is separately accused of sending threatening messages to Edmiston Jr. and remains free on bond pending his case in Wyoming.The Wells investigation itself remains separate from these federal threat cases. No one has been charged with causing Wells' death, and authorities continue to investigate what happened after he disappeared during the July Fourth trip.
Article Summary: A federal judge in Mississippi has ordered Edward James Porter to remain in custody without bond after prosecutors challenged his release. The ruling followed an emergency hearing where an FBI agent described repeated calls and threats allegedly directed at Bart Edmiston Jr. and his family. The threats came weeks after Nolan Wells, 18, disappeared following a Fourth of July trip to Horn Island off Mississippi's Gulf Coast.

Article Title: What happened to Evelyn Lima Dantas? Brazilian TikToker shot and killed at 21
Article Text:
TikToker Evelyn Lima Dantas was reportedly dragged from home before shooting

Evelyn Lima Dantas’ arrest adds another layer to the investigation

A young Brazilian TikToker’s life came to a sudden and violent end after she was reportedly shot outside a home in northern Brazil. Evelyn Lima Dantas, 21, was found dead on Sept. 16 after police responded to reports of gunfire in Mãe do Rio. Her death has raised questions about a possible link to a criminal investigation that had already brought her into police custody earlier this year.Authorities in Mãe do Rio were called early Wednesday after residents heard several gunshots. According to a police report obtained by Brazilian outlet g1, officers arrived at a residential area and found Dantas dead outside a home.Details from her family, as reported to Military Police, paint a disturbing picture of the final moments. Two men allegedly entered the house, took Dantas outside and shot her several times. They then reportedly left the scene in a car.Police also found the letters “TCP” spray-painted at the location. Authorities believe the initials may refer to Terceiro Comando Puro, a criminal faction in Brazil. However, that connection remains part of the investigation and has not been established as a confirmed motive for Dantas’ killing.The case has drawn attention in part because of Dantas’ online presence. She had built a combined audience of more than 150,000 followers on TikTok and her now-deactivated Instagram account. Her posts focused largely on lifestyle, beauty and fitness, giving followers a glimpse into her life away from the criminal investigation surrounding her death.Her TikTok account appeared to have been inactive since January 2025, when she shared a lip-sync video with another creator.Dantas’ recent history with authorities is now another key part of the case. According to the police report cited by g1, she was arrested in July while authorities were investigating the killing of a local police sergeant.She remained in police custody until Sept. 9, when she was released provisionally. Just one week later, she was killed.A Military Police commander said investigators are examining whether her death could have been connected to the earlier case. The official described a possible motive involving retaliation or an attempt to destroy evidence, while stressing that it is one of several investigative possibilities.“We are strongly working with the hypothesis of retaliation or destruction of evidence by some criminal faction,” a Military Police commander told reporters in Spanish of a possible connection between Dantas’s killing and her previous arrest, per g1. “This is one of the main priority lines of investigation and information that we have.”That theory has not been proven, and authorities have yet to publicly establish who was responsible for the killing or why Dantas was targeted.PEOPLE reported that it had contacted the Military Police for comment.As investigators work to piece together what happened, Dantas’ death remains under investigation. The circumstances surrounding her arrest, her release and the shooting are expected to be examined as authorities determine whether the events were connected or whether another motive was involved.
Article Summary: Evelyn Lima Dantas, 21, was found dead on Sept. 16 after police responded to reports of gunfire in Mãe do Rio. Her death has raised questions about a possible link to a criminal investigation that had already brought her into police custody earlier this year.

Article Title: Mohammad Rizwan approaches ICC Anti-Corruption Unit over mobile phone seizure by Pakistan's cyber crime agency
Article Text:
Mohammed Rizwan approaches ICC ACU (Agency Image)

Rizwan seeks clarity over ICC anti-corruption procedures

Lahore High Court dismisses Rizwan’s petition

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NCCIA probe linked to betting and alleged dressing-room leaks

Mohammad Rizwan’s troubles following Pakistan’s England tour have taken another turn, with the wicketkeeper-batter approaching the ICC’s Anti-Corruption Unit (ACU) for clarity over the seizure of his mobile phone by the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA). The move comes days after the Lahore High Court dismissed his petition challenging the agency’s notices, leaving the Pakistan cricketer seeking answers over the handling of his device and the procedures followed during the ongoing inquiry.According to sources quoted by Geo News, Rizwan submitted an online request through the ICC ACU portal, asking whether the ICC or the England and Wales Cricket Board (ECB) was aware of, or involved in, the action taken against him.Sources said Rizwan’s request was not intended as a complaint against any individual or organisation. Instead, the Pakistan batter has sought clarification on the procedures followed in his case and the role, if any, of the ICC or ECB in the seizure of his mobile phone.The former Pakistan white-ball captain has also asked whether the process of requesting his phone, transferring it from England to Pakistan and conducting a forensic examination was in accordance with the ICC Anti-Corruption Code.Rizwan has further sought guidance on his responsibilities and the steps he should follow while cooperating with anti-corruption authorities in the future.The development comes days after the Lahore High Court dismissed Rizwan’s petition challenging notices issued to him by the NCCIA. During Thursday’s hearing, Rizwan’s lawyer, Qazi Umair Ali, told Chief Justice Aalia Neelum that the cricketer had been called to a hotel lobby after the Lord’s Test in England and questioned without being served a notice.According to his counsel, Rizwan’s mobile phone was taken into custody after he was assured that it would be returned within three hours. However, the device has not yet been returned.Rizwan’s lawyer also questioned the NCCIA’s jurisdiction, arguing that the ICC’s Anti-Corruption Unit was the appropriate forum for matters involving alleged corruption-related violations by cricketers. The court directed Rizwan to respond to the NCCIA’s notice before dismissing his petition.The NCCIA notice relates to an inquiry into online betting and gambling in Pakistan cricket. Reports have also linked the investigation to alleged leaks of information from the Pakistan dressing room during the Test series against England.Rizwan and fellow batter Imam-ul-Haq appeared before the agency in Lahore earlier this month as part of the investigation.No final findings against Rizwan or Imam have been officially announced.
Article Summary: Mohammad Rizwan has approached the ICC's Anti-Corruption Unit (ACU) for clarity over the seizure of his mobile phone by the National Cyber Crime Investigation Agency (NCCIA) The move comes days after the Lahore High Court dismissed his petition challenging the agency’s notices. The NCCIA notice relates to an inquiry into online betting and gambling in Pakistan cricket. Reports have also linked the investigation to alleged leaks of information from the Pakistan dressing room.

Article Title: Delhi teen raped, stabbed to death, decomposed body found with hand severed, partly eaten by dogs; 4 held
Article Text:
Police said the girl's decomposed body was found near Jaipal Rana's field on Kushak Road on September 13. (File photo)

(With inputs from PTI)





NEW DELHI: A 17-year-old girl was allegedly raped, stabbed to death and dumped in an open field by four people, including three minors, after she went with them in a tempo, police said on Thursday.The body had decomposed to such an extent that its gender could not be immediately ascertained, they added.According to police, the girl and the accused persons were known to each other. They allegedly drank together inside a tempo before the girl was sexually assaulted, stabbed to death and her body disposed of.Police said the girl's decomposed body was found near Jaipal Rana's field on Kushak Road on September 13.Some parts of the body had also been eaten by stray dogs, while one of her hands was found separated from the body, police added.According to news agency PTI, the girl had not been reported missing by her family. Police said her family told them that she would often leave home and return after a few days.A case was registered under relevant sections of the BNS and the POCSO Act. As there was no apparent eyewitness and the identity of the perpetrators was initially unknown, police teams analysed more than 50 CCTV cameras covering the area and adjoining routes.During the analysis, investigators noticed a tempo moving near the scene around the relevant time.Its registration number was not clearly visible due to darkness, following which investigators tracked its movement across multiple CCTV locations.A night-long search operation was conducted during the intervening night of September 15 and 16, following which the suspected tempo was traced to Khadda Colony in the Swaroop Nagar area. Its driver was identified and questioned.The investigation subsequently led to the apprehension of four persons, including three juveniles, allegedly linked to the crime.The adult accused has been identified as Shivam alias Sudama alias Chuchu, a resident of Khadda Colony, while the three juveniles are aged 16 and 17, police said.Two knives allegedly used in the crime, clothes allegedly worn by the accused and the tempo were recovered.Further investigation is underway to establish the sequence of events, ascertain the individual roles of those apprehended and verify the forensic and technical evidence, police said.
Article Summary: Police said the girl's decomposed body was found near Jaipal Rana's field on Kushak Road on September 13. Some parts of the body had also been eaten by stray dogs, while one of her hands was found separated from the body. The adult accused has been identified as Shivam alias Sudama alias Chuchu.

Article Title: Days after PM Modi’s school friend gets relief in land dispute, Mira-Bhayander Municipal Corporation cancels construction permission to BJP MLA’s company
Article Text:
Mira-Bhayander Municipal Corporation cancelled construction permission for Seven Eleven company.





BHAYANDER: The Mira-Bhayander Municipal Corporation on Wednesday cancelled the construction permission granted to Seven Eleven company, days after BJP MLA Narendra Mehta announced that his company would relinquish possession of the disputed land following the matter being taken up with Prime Minister Narendra Modi In another development, additional tehsildar Nilesh Gaund allowed a petition filed by 81-year-old Asgarali Vohra and ruled against Seven Eleven and other respondents. The order is expected to clear the way for Vohra’s name to be entered in the land records for the property currently in the possession of Seven Eleven, which had fenced off the plot with metal sheets.Vohra had alleged that Mehta and Swayam Builders had illegally encroached on the land at Navghar in Bhayander. He had been pursuing the dispute for around 15 years.On September 8, Vohra approached PM Modi, whom he described as his childhood friend from B N School in Vadnagar in Gujarat, and sought his intervention in the dispute. Soon after, Mehta announced that he would relinquish possession of the property and withdraw a complaint filed against Vohra.On Wednesday, Mehta issued a statement denying that he or his company had cheated anyone.He said the disputed land had been sold to Vohra in 1989 by Renol Lobo and five others. Lobo and the others later sold the land to Swayam Builders in 2011, he said.Mehta further claimed that Seven Eleven had purchased the property through duly registered transactions from Joseph Fernandes and Mukesh Parekh. He said the company decided to return the land to Mukesh Parekh and Mervin Fernandes after a dispute arose over the property.The BJP MLA maintained that surrendering possession and cancelling the transaction was a decision taken to end the dispute and did not amount to an admission of wrongdoing.
Article Summary: Mira-Bhayander Municipal Corporation cancelled construction permission for Seven Eleven company. BJP MLA Narendra Mehta announced that his company would relinquish possession of the disputed land. In another development, additional tehsildar Nilesh Gaund allowed a petition filed by 81-year-old Asgarali Vohra and ruled against Seven Eleven.

Article Title: 36-yr old legal battle lands ex-DGP behind bars
Article Text:
Former state DGP Tomin J Thachankary was sent to Thiruvananthapuram central prison after the court proceedings

Kottayam

:





It was a 36-year-old legal battle pursued by the Karivelithara family of Mithrakari in Alappuzha that resulted in the vigilance court verdict against former DGP Tomin J Thachankary.Though many had given complaints against Thachankary, it was the determined approach of the petitioner Bobby Kuruvila that turned decisive. Though the case against Thachankary had come to a standstill in between, Bobby kept fighting keeping firm belief in the legal system and it finally concluded with Thachankary ending up behind bars.The issues between Thachankary and Bobby’s family traces back to Oct 1990, when Thachankary was serving as assistant superintendent of police in Alappuzha. K L Kuruvila and his sons Bobby and Alexander were charged with attempted murder following a clash with a relative of Thachankary, in which police alleged that they had brandished a firearm. A subsequent complaint to director general of police led crime branch to take over the investigation, which found the attempted-murder allegation to be false, according to the family.Following this, Kuruvila filed a complaint in 1995 alleging that Thachankary had accumulated assets disproportionate to his known income, citing among other evidence an advertisement for a music event organised by Thachankary that had appeared in a Malayalam newspaper in the United States during his police service.Kuruvila died during the course of the legal proceedings, but his sons continued to pursue the case. Bobby reportedly moved Kerala High Court with 12 separate writ petitions, and the matter was also heard by Supreme Court . Vigilance department eventually restricted its probe to the period between Jan 2003 and July 2007, registering a case in 2007. Raids were conducted at six locations, and the investigation concluded in 2013 with a chargesheet filed before Thrissur vVigilance court. The case was later transferred to Muvattupuzha and subsequently to Kottayam, where it was heard until Thursday’s verdict.
Article Summary: Former state DGP Tomin J Thachankary was sent to Thiruvananthapuram central prison after the court proceedings. The case was pursued by the Karivelithara family of Mithrakari in Alappuzha for 36 years.

Article Title: Pune bizman reported 'abducted' from Mumbai airport by wife returns after 'secret' Malaysia trip with woman gets cancelled
Article Text:
A businessman reported missing from Mumbai airport reappeared after his Malaysia trip was cancelled. (Representative image)





MUMBAI: A 46-year-old Pune-based laundry businessman, whose wife had reported him missing from Mumbai International Airport and alleged that he had been abducted, turned up at Sahar police station on Wednesday night, telling police that he had switched off his phone and gone to CST with a female friend after their Malaysia trip was cancelled.The businessman was scheduled to fly to Kuala Lumpur on Monday night for what he had told his family was a "business trip". However, police said he had actually planned to travel with a woman friend. She was stopped during immigration clearance after officials found she was carrying an old passport. The two subsequently cancelled their trip.According to the FIR, earlier that morning, after two friends dropped him at the airport, he called his wife from a landline and claimed that he had surrendered his mobile phone because of an immigration-related issue.At around 3.35pm, he made a WhatsApp video call and told his wife that the issue would soon be resolved. His phone was subsequently switched off and his friends were unable to contact him. Concerned about his whereabouts, his wife approached Sahar police, following which an abduction and kidnapping case was registered.
Article Summary: Pune-based laundry businessman turned up at Sahar police station on Wednesday night. His wife had reported him missing from Mumbai International Airport and alleged that he had been abducted. The businessman was scheduled to fly to Kuala Lumpur on Monday night for what he had told his family was a "business trip"

Article Title: Out on bail, old enmity, 3-4 men in car: How pregnant YouTuber wife’s murder accused was hacked to death
Article Text:
Chithari Haribabu, recently released on bail, was hacked to death by unknown assailants.

'Old enmity'





HYDERABAD: About six months after he was arrested for allegedly killing his pregnant wife, who was also a YouTuber, Chithari Haribabu was hacked to death by a group of unidentified men at Rajarajendra (RR) Centre in Nizamabad on Thursday. He had been out on bail for the past two months.According to B Prasad, ACP, Nizamabad, 26-year-old Haribabu was intercepted by a group of men in a car near Rajarajendra Chowrasta at around 5pm. "Three to four people arrived in a car. One person got out, followed Haribabu and attacked him on the neck and head with a knife used for cutting coconuts," the ACP said. The victim suffered severe injuries and died on the spot. His body was shifted to the govt general hospital, Nizamabad, for postmortem.While police suspect old enmity to be the motive, they have launched an investigation to ascertain the facts. Investigators are also examining whether Haribabu's killing was linked to the murder of his wife, Vaishnavi. On March 17, Vaishnavi, who ran a popular YouTube channel, 'Vaishu Amma', was found dead at her residence in Madhapur village of Korutla mandal, Jagtial, when she was four months pregnant.Her family alleged that Haribabu strangled her and attacked her with a knife following a heated argument between them the previous night. Based on a complaint by Vaishnavi's father, police registered a murder case and arrested Haribabu after taking him into custody on the outskirts of Korutla.Police also booked his mother, Lakshmi, and brothers, Anand and Ashok, for alleged dowry harassment. Haribabu was subsequently released on bail in July."We suspect Vaishnavi's brothers' involvement in this murder but are yet to establish it. We have booked a murder case and are probing all angles to establish the identity of the accused," the ACP added.
Article Summary: Chithari Haribabu, 26, was hacked to death by a group of unidentified men. He had been out on bail for the past two months after being arrested for allegedly killing his pregnant wife, who was also a YouTuber. Police suspect old enmity to be the motive.

Article Title: Apple manager’s murder: 8 years on, 1 cop convicted, another let off
Article Text:
vivek tiwari murder by up police constable at saheed path gomti nagar , residence of vivek tiwari at new hyderabad aakash ganga hospital police constable and other people are gatherd at there residence

Daughters struggle to cope with father’s death

Dissatisfied with verdict, will appeal in higher court: Vivek’s wife





LUCKNOW: Eight years after a 38-year-old Apple area sales manager Vivek Tiwari was allegedly shot dead by two cops in Lucknow, a local court on Thursday convicted constable Prashant Chaudhary of culpable homicide not amounting to murder, while acquitting co-accused constable Sandeep Kumar . The quantum of punishment will be announced on Sept 21.District/sessions judge Malkhan Singh held Prashant Chaudhary guilty under the charges of IPC 304 (culpable homicide not amounting to murder).As per police chargesheet, Prashant was accused of IPC 302 (murder) and co-accused Sandeep of IPC 323 (voluntarily causing hurt).Soon after the judgement was pronounced, both the cops and their kin erupted in joy.Pranshu Agarwal, who represented Vivek Tiwar’s family, told TOI they will go through the detailed judgement and then file an appeal in the high court. “We are awaiting for the judgement copy in the case and also pronouncement of judgement on Sep 21,” said Agarwal.Vivek Tiwari, a resident of New Hyderabad colony, was driving his former colleague Sana Siddiqui to her home in his XUV around 1:30am on Sept 29, 2018. As they reached near Makdoompur outpost in Gomti Nagar Extension, bike-borne cops Prashant Chaudhary and Sandeep signalled them to stop.As Sana lowered the window pane to enquire about the reason, Sandeep hit her with a baton.Vivek did not stop and kept driving. At this, Prashant allegedly took out his service pistol and shot at Vivek, who had barely driven 0.5km ahead.The bullet hit Vivek and he rammed the vehicle on a divider. The two cops fled. Sana sought help from the police control room and took Vivek to Lohia Hospital where he died during treatment.An FIR against the two cops was lodged the next day and the chargesheet against them was filed on Dec 19, 2018. Prashant was charged with murder, while Sandeep was initially charged under Section 323.Vivek’s daughters, aged 15 and 20, still go numb on the mention of his tragic demise. Divyanshi, who was just 7 at the time of incident, had initially been told that her dad was away in Delhi and would return soon. But now the teen girl knows the reality. Priyanshi tries to console her younger sibling every time she breaks down. Divyanshi’s favourite possession is a family drawing she made years ago depicting Vivek, Kalpana, Priyanshi, and herself.Vivek wife Kalpana’s life has been consumed by grief. Every corner of her home is filled with memories of her husband. As she steps into her role as Officer on Special Duty at Nagar Nigam, she carries the weight of her husband’s absence. Kalpana’s brother, Vishnu, said, “He was always there for us, guiding us, helping us. Now, all we want is justice.”Kalpana Tiwari expressed strong dissatisfaction with the verdict and said she would challenge it before a higher court. Speaking after the judgment, she described the decision as disappointing and said the family had expected a harsher punishment.“We had been waiting for the court’s decision since morning and hoped that justice would be delivered. But we are disappointed with the verdict,” Kalpana said, according to the report. She questioned how a trained police constable could have made a mistake while firing his service weapon and maintained that her husband had been shot dead. Kalpana also questioned Sandeep Kumar’s acquittal, saying both constables were present at the spot and, in her view, shared responsibility for the incident.
Article Summary: Vivek Tiwari, 38, was driving his former colleague Sana Siddiqui to her home in his XUV around 1:30am on Sept 29, 2018. As they reached near Makdoompur outpost in Gomti Nagar Extension, bike-borne cops Prashant Chaudhary and Sandeep signalled them to stop. As Sana lowered the window pane to enquire about the reason, Sandeeps hit her with a baton. Vivek did not stop and kept driving.

Article Title: Vizag woman visiting techie son in Melbourne dies after car crashes into Porsche; daughter-in-law killed

Article Title: 'Ab nikaal ke bata gadi': A month before Gurgaon hit-and-run case, men chased, harassed Bhopal biker
Article Text:
In Bhopal, biker Abida Rana encountered a troubling situation when two men in a car relentlessly pursued her on Nabibagh Road





BHOPAL: Nearly a month before a woman biker’s hit-and-run incident in Gurgaon sparked widespread outrage, 23-year-old Bhopal-based biker, Abida Rana, had faced a similar ordeal in the city, with two men in a car chasing her for around 600-700 metres, abusing and repeatedly blocking her way.The ordeal took place on Aug 2 on Nabibagh Road, under Nishatpura police station limits. Abida had shared a video of the Bhopal ordeal on her Instagram handle on Aug 5, which is being widely circulated now.According to Abida, she was around 5 km from home when on the Nishatpura-Nabibagh stretch, two men crossing the road allegedly stopped their car in the middle of the road near the divider and began abusing her without any apparent reason.One of the men allegedly shouted, “Ab nikaal ke bata gadi.” With vehicles behind her honking, Abida said she was forced to move around the car from the left side.The men allegedly changed course and started following her, and repeatedly blocking her way.Abida said she became panicked and angry and told the men that the police station was only 1-2 km away and warned them that she would complain if they continued following and threatening her.When she tried to drive away, the men allegedly blocked her path from the right side as well. She then drove towards the police station, claiming the men continued chasing her and hurling abuses. They left just before the police station.Later, the men were called up to the police station and cops warned the men not to approach her again and made them write an apology before allowing them to leave. No FIR was registered as Abida had opted not to pursue a criminal case, cops said.
Article Summary: Bhopal-based biker Abida Rana, 23, faced a similar ordeal in the city. Two men in a car chased her for around 600-700 metres, abusing and repeatedly blocking her way. Abida had shared a video of the Bhopal ordeal on her Instagram handle.

Article Title: Abandoned pony limping through Kharagpur traffic rescued for veterinary care
Article Text:
A rescued pony, previously abandoned and struggling with severe health issues, was saved from the bustling traffic in Kharagpur





KHARAGPUR: A 7- to 8-year-old skewbald pony found limping through traffic on Kharagpur’s Malancha Road with severely overgrown hooves and other painful health conditions has been rescued and transported to an Animal Rahat sanctuary for veterinary care and rehabilitation. The rescue was carried out following action by People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals India (PETA India), with assistance from West Midnapore district magistrate Bijin Krishna; Superintendent of Police Papiya Sultana; Kharagpur sub-divisional officer Bhuvana Pranith Pappula; Kharagpur Animal Resources Development department deputy director Chinmoy Chakraborty; Kharagpur Town Police Station inspector-in charge Amit Kumar Mitra; and local animal advocate Sudebi Bhattacharya. The operation also received support from Members of Parliament June Maliah and Sayani Ghosh.The abandoned pony was suffering from severely overgrown and enlarged hooves, swollen fetlock joints, chronic osteoarthritis, and impaired mobility. Despite the animal’s evident distress, PETA India personnel faced resistance from certain locals, delaying rescue efforts. The pony was finally secured and taken for treatment after intervention by local authorities and the MPs.“This abandoned pony is yet another victim of the joyride industry. This rescue shows what can be achieved when authorities, animal protection groups, and citizens act together,” said Maliah. “I thank PETA India for never giving up on this pony and Animal Rahat for housing the pony and all the officials led by DM Bijin Krishna and SP Sultana for their prompt intervention in the rescue operation. I urge the public to help other ponies by choosing animal-free forms of entertainment. ”In Kolkata, PETA India continues to campaign for the protection of horses used to haul tourist carriages. In June 2026 alone, the group registered three FIRs involving neglected or distressed horses, including a foal found running frantically through active traffic, a horse with severely overgrown hooves rescued from the Hastings area, and a mare who died in the middle of traffic in Ekbalpore. Since 2024, at least 18 horses in the city have reportedly died or succumbed to injuries from road accidents and other causes.The Calcutta High Court has taken note of the poor condition of horses, the prevalence of unlicensed hackney carriages, and the abandonment of ailing animals. In an order dated May 9, 2024, it directed the state government to develop a proposal to rehabilitate horse-carriage owners so that replacing horse-drawn carriages, as done in Mumbai, can be considered. On July 7, 2026, PETA India appealed for horse-drawn tourist carriages in Kolkata to be replaced with heritage-style electric carriages.PETA India, whose motto reads in part that “animals are not ours to use for entertainment,” opposes speciesism, a human-supremacist worldview.
Article Summary: A 7- to 8-year-old skewbald pony was found limping through traffic on Kharagpur’s Malancha Road. The pony was suffering from severely overgrown and enlarged hooves, swollen fetlock joints, chronic osteoarthritis, and impaired mobility. The rescue was carried out following action by People for the Ethical Treatment of Animals India.

Article Title: Woman dies by suicide; family cites online gaming losses and emotional distress in UP
Article Text:
A 38-year-old woman died by suicide at her Lucknow residence on Wednesday evening (AI image)





LUCKNOW: A 38-year-old woman died by suicide at her residence in Sushant Golf City area on Wednesday evening, with her family attributing the death to severe emotional distress following losses linked to online gaming and the alleged pledging of jewellery without their knowledge.The woman, identified as Vibha Gupta, a resident of Patel Nagar, was found unresponsive inside a room of the house.Inspector Rajeev Ranjan Upadhyay said Vibha’s husband, Rajkumar Gupta , told investigators that she had developed an addiction to online gaming and had lost a substantial amount of money while playing. Family members also informed police that Vibha had allegedly pledged some of her jewellery without informing them. After Rajkumar learned about the financial losses and the jewellery being pledged, he asked her to stop playing online games, they said.According to the family, Vibha remained deeply distressed in the aftermath of the financial losses and related tensions. Police said Rajkumar and Vibha were at home when the incident occurred.Rajkumar, a retired Army personnel, is currently working as a head clerk at Bank of Baroda in Vibhuti Khand. Police recorded statements from family members and are collecting relevant information as part of the inquiry.Family members said Rajkumar was previously married to Sunita Gupta, who died during treatment at Command Hospital in 2000. He has two daughters from the first marriage, Khushboo and Nikki. Rajkumar married Vibha in 2004, and the couple have a 17-year-old son, Atharva.
Article Summary: The woman, identified as Vibha Gupta, a resident of Patel Nagar, was found unresponsive inside a room of the house. Her husband, Rajkumar Gupta, told investigators that she had developed an addiction to online gaming and had lost a substantial amount of money while playing. Family members also informed police that Vibia had allegedly pledged some of her jewellery without informing them.

Article Title: ‘They’re my family’: Bengaluru woman stops crowd from attacking men accused of kidnapping her
Article Text:
Locals attacked a car on Magadi Road, suspecting a kidnapping attempt





BENGALURU: High drama unfolded on Magadi Road Wednesday night after a group of locals allegedly thrashed several men and damaged their car, suspecting they were trying to kidnap a young woman.Six persons, including a nine-year-old girl, sustained injuries in the commotion.However, the alleged kidnapping took a dramatic turn when the woman intervened and told the crowd that the men were her own family members, including her father, who had come from Rajasthan to take her back home.Speaking to police who arrived at the spot, the woman said she had married a man from another caste despite her family’s opposition. She alleged that her family had recently traced her to Bengaluru and was trying to force her to return to Rajasthan.“I’ve married a man from another caste and my family was against it. Recently, we came here and my family somehow followed me,” she told police.A senior police officer said the woman was being requested to lodge a complaint against her family so that action could be taken.Meanwhile, the family’s vehicle was badly damaged after the crowd attacked it. The family members allegedly tried to flee the spot, ramming into other vehicles in the process, officials added.Of those injured, one woman with serious head injuries has been shifted to the ICU of a nearby private hospital, police added. Cops said they are yet to register a case. Suspects have been detained and the car used in the “kidnapping” seized, police said.
Article Summary: Six persons, including a nine-year-old girl, sustained injuries in the commotion. The woman said she had married a man from another caste despite her family’s opposition. She alleged that her family had recently traced her to Bengaluru and was trying to force her to return to Rajasthan.
