Article Title: Rajkot man kills 5-year-old daughter, stores body in fridge; ends life
Article Text:
Police at the house where the murder-suicide took place in Hadida village of Amreli district





RAJKOT: A five-year-old girl was allegedly murdered by her father, who decked up her body and placed it in the refrigerator before taking his own life, in Hadida village of Amreli district’s Savarkundla taluka late on Wednesday night.Preliminary investigation and suicide notes recovered indicated that the 40-year-old man, Kishore Dhanak, took the gruesome step out of financial crisis stemming from investment in a construction site. He allegedly smothered his daughter Himanshi and then hanged himself to death in another room.Late on Wednesday night, Hadida sarpanch called the police, informing them about the deaths. When cops reached there, they found Dhanak hanging and three suicide notes on the cot.One of the notes mentioned that he had killed his daughter and placed the body in the refrigerator.His wife Manju had gone to her aunt’s house on Sept 14. When she returned the next day, she found the house locked. Dhanak told her on the phone that he was at a friend’s house in Mahuva and asked her to go to her parental home in Dadhia.On Sept 16, he told Manju that he had gone to Mahuva in adjoining Bhavnagar district to collect money and later asked her to start for home.When he did not contact her again till evening, she sent her brother Ghanshyam to check on them. Ghanshyam found the house locked and received no response despite calling out to them.Manju, her brother and father subsequently reached the house. After being alerted by a neighbour, the sarpanch was called and the door was opened.In one note, Dhanak referred to around Rs 7.25 lakh due to him from the construction project and said he had also invested personal loan money in it.In another note, he reportedly admitted to killing his daughter by covering her mouth and said he did so because he feared she would suffer without him. The third note contained an apology and, on its reverse side, reportedly stated that he had kept his daughter’s body in the refrigerator.Police also found that Dhanak had worn gloves on his hands and feet and covered his face with a cloth before taking his own life.Girl’s head covered with chunri, tulsi leaves placed in mouthPL Chaudhary, inspector, Savarkundla Rural police station, said when the girl’s body was recovered from the refrigerator, her father had placed tulsi leaves in her mouth, covered her head with a chunri and put a garland around her neck. “There were signs of some kind of celebration in the room where Dhanak was found hanging. The room had been decorated with colourful balloons and kites,” he said.Investigators are now examining whether Dhanak had celebrated an occasion with his daughter shortly before allegedly killing her, and are trying to establish what happened in the house before the tragedy.
Article Summary: Kishore Dhanak, 40, allegedly smothered his daughter Himanshi and then hanged himself to death in another room. He took the gruesome step out of financial crisis stemming from investment in a construction site. His wife Manju had gone to her aunt’s house on Sept 14 and found the house locked.

Article Title: ‘2 shots, sacked ex-colleague, financial dispute’: Inside Delhi HR professional’s killing
Article Text:
31-year-old HR professional Yuvraj Singh Manchanda

Family lost contact after Gurgaon meeting

Call records, CCTV led police to Anya

Body recovered from Gurgaon drain





NEW DELHI: Police are probing the killing of a 31-year-old HR professional who went to Gurgaon on September 6 to meet his former colleague Anya Vats, was shot twice inside his own car and his body was kept in the vehicle for at least seven hours before being dumped in a drain, while the accused fled to Uttarakhand.Police have arrested Anya Vats and her partner Sanyam Sachdeva, both from Gurgaon, in connection with the alleged murder and produced in court, which sent them to five days’ police custody.Yuvraj had gone to a restaurant in Lajpat Nagar around 4pm on September 6. His family said he had gone shopping with his sisters before visiting the restaurant. He later told them he had a meeting in Gurgaon and asked his sisters to take a cab home before leaving.According to the complaint, the family spoke to Yuvraj around 7pm, when he said he would return home by 10pm. His phone then appeared to be switched off and the family could not reach him.His sister approached Lajpat Nagar police on September 11, following which a missing-person FIR was registered.Investigators analysed call detail records, internet protocol data and CCTV footage and found that Yuvraj had last spoken to Anya.He had also told his family that he was going to Gurgaon to meet her.Both Yuvraj’s and Anya’s phones were switched off, prompting investigators to track Anya’s movements. She subsequently emerged as a prime suspect.Investigators later detected a new mobile number allegedly being used by Anya. Technical surveillance indicated that she was in Uttarakhand. A police team was sent there, where Anya and Sanyam were apprehended.Police said the two disclosed their involvement in the murder and told investigators that they had thrown Yuvraj’s body into a drain near their house in Gurgaon.The disclosure led investigators to Badshahpur police station in Gurgaon, where an unidentified body was found in a drain on September 10. The body was badly decomposed.Police showed photographs of the body to Yuvraj’s family, who identified him.Police suspect a financial dispute to be behind the killing. Anya had worked with Yuvraj in 2022 at another prominent real estate developer’s office and was currently unemployed. Police said she was sacked from the company and that some financial irregularities may have been the reason for her termination, though this is being verified. Sanyam was also unemployed.Police are investigating the circumstances surrounding the killing, the alleged financial dispute, the exact roles of the accused and other aspects of the case, besides collecting forensic and technical evidence.
Article Summary: Yuvraj Singh Manchanda, 31, went to Gurgaon on September 6 to meet his former colleague Anya Vats. He was shot twice inside his own car and his body was kept in the vehicle for at least seven hours before being dumped in a drain. Police have arrested Anya and her partner Sanyam Sachdeva in connection with the alleged murder and sent them to five days' police custody.

Article Title: After meeting govt delegation, Manoj Jarange calls off hunger strike on 20th day of agitation, gives govt another three months
Article Text:
Manoj Jarange ended his 20-day hunger strike after government talks.





CHHATRAPATI SAMBHAJINAGAR: Maratha quota activist Manoj Jarange on Thursday morning called off his indefinite hunger strike on its 20th day after a government delegation held talks with him at Patoda in Beed district and sought three months to address his key demands. This was Jarange’s 11th agitation over the past three years.Cabinet ministers Radhakrishna Vikhe Patil and Dada Bhuse, along with BJP MLA from Ashti Suresh Dhas and BJP MLC Prasad Lad, reached Patoda around 5.40am to discuss Jarange’s demands on behalf of the govt. Following the talks, Jarange announced that he was suspending his fast for 90 days, saying there had been positive discussions on his five main demands.Jarange said the suspension of the hunger strike did not mean the end of his agitation. He gave the government three months to issue the necessary government resolution and implement the Gazetteer-related measures. He also demanded a written assurance that not a single record would be deleted from the nearly 58 lakh records identified in the process of establishing Maratha-Kunbi links.“If the government betrays us, we will go to Mumbai,” Jarange warned, while appealing to over 1 lakh of his supporters who according to him had travelled towards Mumbai, to return home.He said he was prepared to trust the government for three months following the discussions at Patoda.Before announcing the suspension of his fast, Jarange also said Chief Minister Devendra Fadnavis was not his enemy and indicated that he would continue to maintain affection for Deputy Chief Minister Eknath Shinde, while making it clear that he would not compromise on the demands of the Maratha community.After ending his fast, Jarange left Patoda for a private hospital in Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar city, where he had been undergoing treatment periodically for the past three years.
Article Summary: Manoj Jarange ended his 20-day hunger strike after government talks. Jarange said the suspension of the hunger strike did not mean the end of his agitation. He gave the government three months to issue the necessary government resolution and implement the Gazetteer-related measures.

Article Title: UP man beheads sleeping wife over ‘affair’, walks into police station

Article Title: Another hit-and-run in Delhi-NCR: Man collecting birthday cake hit by speeding SUV in Greater Noida, suffers spine fracture
Article Text:
A speeding car struck a pedestrian near Ek Murti Chowk, causing serious injuries





NOIDA: A 32-year-old man suffered several fractures in a hit-and-run accident at Ek Murti Chowk in Greater Noida earlier this month. A video of the accident recorded by a rear-view camera of a car shows that the collision impact flung the man into the air.Police have arrested the driver, a 24-year-old management student, on Sept 14 and impounded the car.According to a complaint filed by the victim, Himanshu Rai, at the Bisrakh police station, the accident took place at around 4.35 am on Sept 5. He told the cops, “It was my birthday, so after work my wife and I had gone out.”He collected a pre-ordered cake from a bakery and was crossing the road at the chowk when a white SUV, driven at high speed, rammed him.“The car hit me at what appeared to be a speed of over 100 km per hour and drove away. The way the car was being driven, it seemed that the driver might have been under the influence of alcohol,” he said.People in the vicinity rushed to his aid and took him to a hospital for treatment.The man sustained fractures to his legs, hand and knees, besides suffering a fracture to his spine. He is currently undergoing treatment at the hospital.Police subsequently traced the vehicle and initiated action against the driver, Priyanshu. The Tata Punch allegedly involved in the accident was taken into custody.A case has been registered against him under BNS sections 125(b) (act endangering life or personal safety) and 281 (rash driving).The accident comes at the heel of a hit and run incident in Gurgaon where a biker was chased down by a group of men on Golf Course Road.Kalyan Bainsla (33), who rammed his car into Shivani Chauhan’s bike and caused her to fall in the middle of fast-moving traffic on Golf Course Road Sunday morning, was arrested at Dausa in Rajasthan on Tuesday.A video from her bike’s camera that Chauhan uploaded online showed her being knocked down near Sector 55-56 Rapid Metro station after the car repeatedly tried to get alongside her bike.Her Aprilia RS 457 slid across the road, while traffic sped past her.Bainsla’s cousin Lovneesh (32), who was in the Maruti Ciaz with him on Sunday, was arrested too. After examining the video of the crash that Shivani shared, police have added the attempt to murder charge in the FIR against Bainsla.“He caused the collision deliberately from the side. He had an intention to kill her,” DCP (east) Sandeep Kumar said
Article Summary: A 32-year-old man suffered several fractures in a hit-and-run accident at Ek Murti Chowk in Greater Noida earlier this month. A video of the accident recorded by a rear-view camera of a car shows that the collision impact flung the man into the air. The incident comes at the heel of a hit and run incident in Gurgaon where a biker was chased down.

Article Title: Palantir CEO Alex Karp wants US government to take over OpenAI, Anthropic; says else every client of mine will sue them as ...
Article Text:
US government oppose some tech leaders’ demand

‘New’ operational failures and mounting legal scrutiny

Palantir CEO Alex Karp has taken a strong stand, urging the US government to step in and nationalise leading artificial intelligence (AI) research labs. He warned that failure to establish state control may result in a wave of private litigation against developers. As per CNBC, Karp stated that authorities must set reasonable and practical guidelines around machine learning systems, emphasising that direct legal liability remains the primary safeguard against corporate negligence, arguing that developers should face both criminal charges and civil damages whenever irresponsible engineering leads to public harm.Karp was explicit about why he believes advanced AI companies may ultimately have to be taken over by the state: “The view that I believe they have is, these businesses have to be nationalized because if you don’t nationalize it every single one of my clients is going to sue.”Karp’s demands arrive at a time when there is a debate among industry titans and the government officials regarding how to govern AI tools, sparked by warnings from computer scientists and researchers about the threat to humanity.Recently, Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei demanded a slowdown in frontier model development. His stand gained swift backing from OpenAI CEO Sam Altman as well as Tesla and SpaceX boss Elon Musk. However, President Donald Trump aggressively rejected the warnings, posting multiple messages on social media dismissing AI dangers as a “hoax.”Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Meta’s Mark Zuckerberg have similarly challenged these narratives. Writing on X, Zuckerberg cautioned that research labs that fail to prioritise alignment will simply lose ground to competitors.Adding fuel to the debate, OpenAI revealed that it had recorded six separate instances of alarming or unexpected model operations over the last few months. Those disclosures arrive alongside the high-profile security compromise of developer hub Hugging Face, which reignited debate over whether safety checks are adequate.Addressing the flurry of software missteps, Karp insisted that the tech sector must get serious about operational safeguards.
Article Summary: Palantir CEO Alex Karp has called on the US government to nationalise leading AI research labs. He warned that failure to establish state control may result in a wave of private litigation against developers. Karp’s demands arrive at a time when there is a debate among industry titans and government officials regarding how to govern AI tools.

Article Title: While most Americans may hate datacenters, UAE minister calls them 'more important than roads'; and has a new ‘hiding rule’ for them after war destroyed many
Article Text:
Representative Image

How Iran war changed how UAE deals with data centers 'forever'

'One country regulating AI will not work, it has to be almost the entire world'

The United Arab Emirates (UAE) will overhaul its regulatory framework for data centres and halt public disclosure of their physical locations to shield them from military threats, according to comments reported by The Next Web of a session from Salesforce's annual event Dreamforce 2026. Speaking alongside Salesforce CEO Marc Benioff at the Dreamforce conference in San Francisco, Omar Sultan Al Olama, the UAE’s Minister of State for Artificial Intelligence, Digital Economy and Remote Work Applications, warned that computing hubs have evolved into critical infrastructure that requires heightened protection.Al Olama said that data centres have become prime targets because our whole lives exist on connected devices, arguing that they are now more important than bridges, roads, or tunnels. In remarks highlighted in the 'The Next Web' report, the minister stated that the UAE will no longer promote the locations of these facilities to prevent bad actors from targeting them, adding that he expects other nations will soon be forced to adopt similar measures. "Unfortunately they’re more important than bridges. They’re more important than roads. They’re more important than tunnels because our whole lives are on these devices that we’re using," said Al Olama, in a session Salesforce published.Incidentally, UAE minister's views are very different from that of most Americans. While Donald Trump government strongly supports data centres, most states across the US are not in strong favour of them. The debate around data center projects is one of the rare modern issues to cut across party lines, demographics and geography -- uniting the US. As a report in AP says, from Republican-dominated Nebraska, Texas and Wyoming to swing-state Pennsylvania to Democratic-leaning New Mexico, in a divided America, the left and right unite to oppose AI data centers.The strategic shift comes in the wake of severe regional conflict that began on February 28, a day Al Olama recalled preparing for a trip to Ecuador before hostilities escalated. The UAE faced more than 1,000 projectiles and drones during the first week of the conflict alone, with launches from Iran taking only two minutes to reach the country. Al Olama noted that the UAE intercepted more aerial threats than the entire Middle East and Israel combined, resulting in zero impact on human lives or business operations. Domestic life has since returned to normal, though the government is now decentralizing key digital assets, including splitting up its domestic Stargate data centre project and investing in offshore facilities, such as in Germany.Reflecting on broader AI policy, Al Olama warned against allowing fear to choke innovation, drawing a historical parallel to the Middle East’s technological decline after centuries of dominance from 813 to 1515 AD. That era ended when the region banned the Gutenberg printing press for two centuries due to fears over misinformation, alterations to holy scripture, and general administrative anxiety. He cautioned that modern leaders cannot afford to repeat that mistake with artificial intelligence, even if the technology's rapid evolution initially seems frightening.When it comes to public deployment, Al Olama advocated a measured approach that avoids unproven, high-risk systems. UAE public services, such as Abu Dhabi’s TAMM administrative platform, run on established, older large language models rather than cutting-edge frontier systems like OpenAI’s Astra or Anthropic’s Fable, which he warned carry significant cybersecurity and data breach risks. He also drew hard red lines against using AI for predictive policing, citing the danger of false positives, and cautioned against building an oppressive surveillance apparatus, pointing instead to quality-of-life improvements like desk-free biometric airport transit.To insulate the domestic workforce from technological displacement, the UAE has trained all 80,000 federal civil servants in agentic AI, following an earlier initiative that taught prompt design to one million people. Al Olama dismissed fears of mass unemployment, insisting the technology will ultimately create opportunities and boost workforce capability.Addressing the global regulatory landscape, Al Olama noted that governments typically overregulate while the private sector tends to underregulate. He pointed to the UAE’s own data protection laws, which were initially drafted by tech companies before state officials and civil society refined them, as a model for collaborative oversight. He warned Western policymakers that unilateral bans on AI would simply hand an insurmountable advantage to competitors, arguing that restrictions in the United States make little sense unless China agrees to follow suit.
Article Summary: Omar Sultan Al Olama, the UAE’s Minister of State for Artificial Intelligence, Digital Economy and Remote Work Applications, warned that computing hubs have evolved into critical infrastructure that require heightened protection. He said the UAE will no longer promote the locations of these facilities to prevent bad actors from targeting them.

Article Title: Hazaribag man drowns while fishing in lake

Article Title: FIR filed against 2 Enforcement Directorate officers from Jaipur for extorting Rs 2.25 crore from Mumbai businessman
Article Text:
The crime branch has been tasked to carry out the investigation

Mumbai:





An FIR has been registered at Bangur Nagar police station in Goregaon after the Enforcement Directorate (ED) accused two of its officials posted in Jaipur of threatening and extorting Rs 2.25 crore from a Mumbai businessman.Mumbai crime branch has been tasked to investigate the case.Amulya Vassa, proprietor of Wintree Tech Pvt Ltd, had complained that on July 20, around 3pm, two men, who identified themselves as Jaipur ED’s assistant director Mohit Garg (36) and enforcement officer Devendra Gupta (35), visited his office at Ken Plaza, Mindspace in Malad West. They questioned him about his business and accused him of dealing in proceeds of crime. The duo did not produce documents supporting the allegations, but threatened a search-and-seizure operation, Vassa claimed.The complaint alleged that the two men threatened to damage Vassa’s reputation and referred to information about his personal life and associates. One of them allegedly instructed him to keep two high-end phones and SIM cards ready for them and took a phone and SIM card registered in an employee’s name.“Vassa alleged that the ED officer initially demanded Rs 5 crore, but settled for Rs 2.25 crore. He allegedly told Vassa that failure to pay could result in strict action and arrest. Later that evening, the complainant and his business associate accompanied the accused to a restaurant in Malad, where the discussions continued. Vassa said he handed over Rs 1 crore the following day,’’ said a police officer.The accused then claimed that the matter had been approved for closure by senior officials. When Vassa sought documentary proof, they told him that the file could only be verified physically in Delhi. On July 25, two of Vassa’s associates allegedly met the accused at a mall in Delhi. They were allegedly shown a document indicating that the matter had been settled, following which the remaining Rs 1.25 crore was paid.The complaint stated that the accused subsequently demanded additional money, claiming that senior officials were unhappy and needed to be paid. They allegedly also sought regular monthly payments, stated the FIR.Vassa later examined the documents and after making enquiries through acquaintances realised that he had been cheated and that the duo had extorted Rs 2.25 crore from him.Crime branch officers said the ED filed the FIR after a preliminary inquiry found that the two men named in the complaint were actually its officials.The complaint alleged that Garg and Gupta, while working as ED officials, misused their positions and the authority of the agency, conspired to intimidate Vassa by falsely portraying him as being involved in transactions involving proceeds of crime, and demanded and accepted Rs 2.25 crore.

Article Title: State punishment for cop who flouts rules: Bombay HC on Palghar hospital attack
Article Text:
Bombay high court

Mumbai:





Bombay high court on Thursday asked the state DGP to submit a report on what form of punishment is applicable to a police officer who violates rules and circulars on procedures when carrying out an investigation.The DGP is to inform HC by Oct 9 whether the punishment is to be a ‘minor’ one, such as withholding of remuneration for three years, or a more serious kind of action can be initiated, said a bench of Justices A S Gadkari and Kamal Khata.HC set aside a show-cause notice issued by Palghar SP issued to an SI for not maintaining a proper record, including the station diary, in a probe over the alleged assault of a Palghar hospital staffer on Sept 5 over the treatment of some govindas injured during a dahi handi celebration. The notice had asked the SI to show why he should not be punished by stopping his remuneration for three years.The bench observed that it regularly comes across such cases.On Sept 11, HC had expressed its displeasure at the “lackadaisical manner” in which the investigation was carried out. “A bare perusal of spot panchnama/scene of offence panchnama prima facie indicates that it is good for nothing,” it had said.On Thursday, state public prosecutor Shishir Hiray said the SI was issued a show-cause notice.HC said the state was unable to cite the exact provision based on which the three-year punishment was proposed. Hiray cited the provision under the Maharashtra police manual.Senior counsel Ashok Mundargi, amicus Curiae (friend of court), said 22 arrests have been shown in the case and he hoped they did not include the govindas who had sought treatment. Hiray said the govindas were not among those arrested.Meanwhile, HC was informed in the suo motu PIL in the Dombivli doctors’ assault case that charges have been framed in the case and the trial would be expedited.Indian Medical Association, through its senior counsel S U Kamdar, had earlier said assaulting doctors and hospital staffers performing their duties is a very sensitive issue. “It has now become a trend among people to take the law into their hands. Some unscrupulous elements of society use this practice to exhibit their prowess over helpless and vulnerable doctors and hospital staff,” it had said.
Article Summary: HC set aside a show-cause notice issued by Palghar SP issued to an SI for not maintaining a proper record. The notice had asked the SI to show why he should not be punished by stopping his remuneration for three years. HC said the state was unable to cite the exact provision based on which the three-year punishment was proposed.
